title: SLAS Technology paper applies acoustic ejection MS to covalent BTK inhibitor screening
summary: Cheng, Muneer and Hercher used acoustic ejection mass spectrometry as a high-throughput pipeline for covalent inhibitor screening, reactivity profiling and potency analysis, with BTK as model target.

claims.text: Pipeline covers ultra-high-throughput screening, reactivity profiling and potency analysis
BTK used as the model target

why_it_matters: Shows acoustic ejection MS moving from plate readout to a full assay pipeline, the same route high-throughput ADME is taking.

title: Hu and Blair: acoustic ejection MS analyses reactions without chromatography (Nature)
summary: St. Jude Nature paper analyses reactions by starting-material fragmentation patterns instead of chromatography, enabling fast multiplexed reaction screening.

claims.text: Reaction screening, not ADME; plate size not confirmed from abstract

why_it_matters: Chromatography-free MS is the enabling trick for fast ADME readouts too; reaction work is the proof of concept, not ADME itself.

title: SCIEX claims Echo MS cuts metabolic-stability analysis time about 10x versus LC-MS/MS
summary: SCIEX tech notes claim up to 10x throughput versus LC-MS/MS for metabolic stability, and up to 60x (2 s per sample) with Echo MS+ on ZenoTOF 7600. No independent validation found.

claims.text: Up to 10x vs LC-MS/MS, 23 compounds, human and rat microsomes (vendor note)
Echo MS+ note: up to 60x, 2 s vs 2 min per sample; baselines differ between notes
Vendor-reported best cases; undated notes (published date is a placeholder)

why_it_matters: If it holds, the bottleneck in HT-ADME shifts from MS time to incubation and liquid handling. Vendor claims, so validate in-house.
